verdict: NOT STATED UNAMBIGUOUSLY. The source gives the flash only qualitatively: 10 ms, white, 'bright', 'saturating', after 5-15 s dark adaptation, from an uncalibrated (in photons) 100-lumen white LED. It does not state the ND attenuation, so it is not even stated that the flash was the unattenuated source (logI 0).

bounded_range.lower_bound: the flash is SATURATING (Supp. Note I.1): it is at least the light level at which the R1-R6 flash response saturates. In engine units this is E_sat below.
bounded_range.upper_bound: the unattenuated rig output (logI 0, 'daylight'), which is not calibrated in photons in the source and therefore has no engine value. The engine grid's top (encoder 10,000 = 100 x JH2001 BG0, ~3e8 effective photons/s) is used as a NOMINAL stand-in for reporting only.
bounded_range.not_used: JH2001's BG0 (~3e6 effective photons/s) is the engine's intensity UNIT, not a property of Mansour's flash (different rig, a steady background not a flash). v8's encoder 330 (3.3 x BG0) was an assumption and is retired.

engine_units: BrainV6 light intensity I is in units of JH2001 BG0 (~3e6 effective photons/s); encoder level = I / encoder_to_intensity with encoder_to_intensity = 0.01 (S1-A3, FIXED, not changed in v9). So encoder 100 = 1 x BG0.

conversion_rule_prestated.name: E_sat (saturation-threshold mapping)
conversion_rule_prestated.rule: E_sat = the LOWEST encoder level on the half-log grid {10^(k/2), k = 0..8} = {1, 3.16, 10, 31.6, 100, 316, 1000, 3162, 10000} at which the R1-R6 flash peak deflection (10 ms flash after 10 s dark, v8 protocol and measurement) is >= 0.90 x the peak deflection at encoder 10,000.
conversion_rule_prestated.evaluated_once_at: the v8 base photoreceptor (S1-A3: G, Ka, Kt, tau_p0_ms, tau_a_ms, n_stages; encoder_to_intensity 0.01) with dead time 7 ms, by the v9 probe (scripts/v9/probe_v9.py). E_sat is then FIXED for the whole v9 fit (it does not move with fitted parameters).
conversion_rule_prestated.why_this_bound: The source's only quantitative handle is 'saturating', which defines a lower bound. Within the engine (and in v8's run-0 descriptive curve: encoder 330 -> 14 ms, 33 -> 20, 3.3 -> 25) brighter flashes give EARLIER peaks, so E_sat is the source-consistent level most LENIENT to a slow R peak. A G1 FAIL at E_sat therefore holds for every source-consistent level (if the probe confirms monotonicity); a G1 PASS at E_sat is CONDITIONAL on the real flash being near the saturation threshold. This asymmetry is pre-stated.
conversion_rule_prestated.validity_check: G0 (v9 prereg): for each run's final parameters, the flash at E_sat must still be >= 0.90 saturating (same definition). If the probe shows that E_sat varies across the free-parameter box, this is disclosed in the prereg before freezing.
conversion_rule_prestated.disclosure: The analyst knows v8's run-0 intensity -> time-to-peak curve (acceptance note). The rule was chosen from the source wording before the v9 probe and does not reference 25.5 ms.
